name: @vigilia/scene-fabric
description: Renders a ScenePlan onto a Fabric canvas. Shared by the display-only player and the editor.
//sideEffects: Declared explicitly because both are real and both fail SILENTLY if dropped. chart-engine.ts is a bare `echarts.use(...)` import and a missing registration does not throw — the chart just draws nothing. chart-object.ts ends with `classRegistry.setClass`, without which loadFromJSON cannot revive a chart. Setting `"sideEffects": false` here to shrink a bundle would remove both. `chart-object.dom.test.ts` mounts all four families, which is what would catch it.
//: This package exists so that Fabric is NOT reachable from @vigilia/renderer-core, whose barrel the Node host imports runtime values from. Two rules, both enforced by packages/player/src/boundaries.test.ts rather than by this comment: import Fabric only from the 'fabric/es' subpath (the default entry is one pre-bundled file no tree-shaker can see into, measured at 95.0 KB gzip against 49.3 KB), and never the interactive `Canvas` (+31.0 KB the player cannot use) — the adapter takes a StaticCanvas and @vigilia/editor constructs the interactive one.
